docs.agreement.p1: The first time Handscore opens, it shows its licence agreement. Until you choose Agree, Handscore does nothing and makes no sound.
docs.agreement.p2: Your answer is kept on your computer and shared by every open copy of Handscore, in every DAW and in the standalone app. If you decline, the agreement stays on screen, ready for whenever you agree.
docs.agreement.title: The licence agreement
docs.classics.p1: Select Mode's Classics hold sixty-two public-domain songs to learn: nursery songs, Christmas songs and carols, folk songs, spirituals and anthems, classical themes and piano favourites. Each is arranged for two hands, the melody in the right and the chords in the left. Search by title or composer, then choose Play.
docs.classics.p2: A classic is yours to learn, never to take: only its chords may leave Handscore. A generated song whose melody, counter-melody or bassline matches a well-known tune keeps that part in, and says why.
docs.classics.title: The classics
docs.drag.p1: Drag a part from its sheet, or the whole song with Drag all, straight into your DAW as MIDI. Export saves the MIDI of a part or the whole song to a file you name, with every note's velocity, each part's level and pan, the tempo and the time signature.
docs.drag.p2: Export to PDF writes the sheets with a cover page: the title, tempo, key and scale, length, bars, the notes in total, per part and per page, and the instruments. Add credits — writers, vocalists, producers, the samples you used and where they came from, the record label — with names suggested as you type.
docs.drag.title: Into your DAW
docs.edit.p1: Stage, Melody, Chords, Counter and Bassline run along the top. A part's tab opens its own piano roll, with a mute dot, Solo and a × that clears the part. Select, move, lengthen, delete, copy, paste and clone notes; right-click and drag to take notes away and bring them back. Each part has its own gain and pan.
docs.edit.p2: Record from a MIDI keyboard into the roll after a count-in of one or two bars. Fold a roll to the song's scale, or to the rows that hold notes: the scale's rows are tinted and a note outside it is marked. As you draw, the next note or chord is suggested faintly; Tab keeps it, a click keeps one, and drawing elsewhere clears it.
docs.edit.p3: Switch on Chords beside the transport and one key plays a chord of 3, 4 or 5 notes in the song's key, from the mouse, the computer keyboard or a MIDI keyboard.
docs.edit.title: Editing the notes
docs.generate.p1: The panel on the left (its tab on the window's edge shows and hides it) searches 73 genres, 1,507 artists and 833 producers. Choose one and press Generate, or G: four parts — chords, melody, counter-melody and bassline — are written in that style, 4 or 8 bars long, and the hands play them on the piano.
docs.generate.p2: The chips beside Generate set the key, the scale (41 of them), the mood, the tempo (20 to 999 BPM; drag up or down on the number), the complexity and 4 or 8 bars, and each shows what the song was made in. Follow DAW writes at your project's tempo. Playable voices the parts for two hands; Raw keeps them exactly as written.
docs.generate.title: Generating a song
docs.hands.p1: Two realistic hands play every note on the stage, the way a pianist would: each finger chosen for the passage, the thumb passing under on a scale, wide chords reached, and a hand lifting up and over the other when the music crosses. When nothing plays they rest on the keys, ready.
docs.hands.p2: Handscore works out which hand plays each note, and with which finger, before the music plays, so the hands arrive as the keys go down.
docs.hands.title: The hands
docs.intro: Handscore is growing into realistic hands on every family of instruments, with music lessons from the piano to finger drumming, songwriting and song arrangement. This manual grows with it, version by version. Right now it covers what version 0.4.0 does: the pianos and the hands, generating a song, the sheets, the drag and export, the editor, the classics and the transport.
docs.language.p1: Handscore speaks eighteen languages and starts in your system's language.
docs.language.title: Languages
docs.lyrics.p1: Type words under the melody or the counter-melody, the syllables marked: they are printed on the sheet and lit as they are sung. A counter beside each line shows whether it fits its bar. As you type, the rest of the word is suggested (Tab takes it) and a misspelling is corrected, unless you tap the checkmark or press Shift+Tab to keep your word.
docs.lyrics.title: Lyrics
docs.pianos.p1: Four pianos take the stage one at a time: Grand Piano, Acoustic Piano, Upright Piano and Honky-Tonk Piano, each with its own shape, finish and sound.
docs.pianos.p2: The Select Mode button at the top left (or P) opens your choices by category. Under Instruments, Preview plays a short phrase on a piano without switching, and Choose puts it on the stage, crossfading from the last one. Your choice is saved with your project.
docs.pianos.title: The pianos
docs.play.p1: Click a key to hear it, or slide across the keys to play each in turn. Each key goes down on its balance rail, faster the harder it is played, and its name fades while it is down and comes back when it rises.
docs.play.p2: MIDI from your DAW plays the piano and moves its keys. The sustain pedal holds the notes you let go until you lift it.
docs.play.title: Playing the keys
docs.privacy.p1: The plugin and the standalone app never use the network. If Handscore ever stops unexpectedly, a short report is kept on your computer and offered the next time it opens; nothing is sent unless you choose to report it.
docs.privacy.title: Your privacy
docs.project.p1: Saving your DAW project keeps the song, its edits, its mix, its words, the piano, the view and the credits, and reopening it brings them back as they were.
docs.project.title: Your project
docs.seeds.p1: Every generation shows its seed, and each part its take seed, with Copy. Paste a song's seed to make that song again, or a part's take seed to bring that take back. Back and Forward step through every generation you have made, each brought back exactly and kept across restarts; a new generation never repeats an old one.
docs.seeds.title: Seeds and history
docs.sheets.p1: Each part is printed as a page of sheet music on the piano's music desk, with its title and page number, and a full score of all the parts stands beside them. Every note head lights as it sounds under a moving playhead, and a long part turns its pages as it plays. Click a sheet, or press 1 to 5, to bring it close; Esc goes back.
docs.sheets.title: The sheets
docs.shortcuts.p1: Press ? or the Shortcuts key in the top bar to see every shortcut.
docs.shortcuts.title: Keyboard shortcuts
docs.stage.p1: Below the top bar is the stage: the piano you chose, its 88 keys, A0 to C8, at a real piano's measurements, filling the width of the window. Every key's name is on its front — white keys in dark ink, black keys in white — and hides while the key is down, so you can always see which notes are being played.
docs.stage.p2: If your computer cannot draw in 3D, the stage says so and explains how to turn it on, instead of showing nothing.
docs.stage.p3: Handscore measures how fast your computer draws the stage and settles on the quality it can hold smoothly.
docs.stage.title: The stage
docs.start.p1: Handscore runs inside your DAW as a CLAP, VST3 or AU instrument, or on its own as a standalone app. Put it on an instrument track.
docs.start.p2: There are no downloads before version 1.0.0, and the source code is private.
docs.start.title: Getting started
docs.theme.p1: The Dark theme switch at the top right turns the window light or dark. Handscore remembers your choice, and so do the other Freally apps on your computer.
docs.theme.title: Light and dark
docs.transport.p1: Under the stage: rewind, play or pause, stop and fast-forward, and a timeline with the song's time and a mark at every bar. Hover over the timeline to see the hands at that moment in a small preview; click or drag to go there. Hold rewind or fast-forward to move quickly. Either way you hear every note you pass. Space plays and pauses, and the arrow keys on the timeline step a bar.
docs.transport.p2: The M beside the keys is the metronome. Switch it on and a click marks each beat, the first of every bar higher, while its two dots show the beat.
docs.transport.p3: When a song has words, the timeline's preview shows the ones being sung at that moment.
docs.transport.title: The transport
docs.tray.p1: Under the stage, the tray holds each part with Solo, Mute, Lock and a new take. A locked part stays when you generate again. Take, Dream 1–3 and Re-Dream offer three new versions of a part beside the one you have: pick one and keep it.
docs.tray.title: The sheet tray
featuresPage.cards.classics.body: Public-domain songs to learn, from nursery songs and carols to anthems and classical themes, each arranged for two hands and played by the hands on the stage. Only their chords can ever leave Handscore.
featuresPage.cards.classics.title: The classics
featuresPage.cards.daw.body: CLAP and VST3 on Windows, macOS and Linux, AU on macOS, and a standalone app for working without a DAW.
featuresPage.cards.daw.title: In any DAW
featuresPage.cards.drag.body: One part at a time or all four together, dragged from the sheets straight into your DAW, or saved as a MIDI file or as a PDF of the sheets.
featuresPage.cards.drag.title: Drag the MIDI
featuresPage.cards.drums.body: A pad controller played by realistic hands, every pad lit as it is hit. Generate a drum pattern or play your own in, loop it and add to it, and learn from the first beat to full grooves.
featuresPage.cards.drums.title: Finger drumming
featuresPage.cards.hands.body: Two hands that play every note the way a player would: the finger a pianist would choose, the fret and the stroke a guitarist would use.
featuresPage.cards.hands.title: Realistic hands
featuresPage.cards.lessons.body: A piano course from Day 1 that listens as you play and moves on when you have it right, then courses in reading music, rhythm, ear training, theory, songwriting and lyrics, song arrangement and mixing. Switch Read Aloud on and each lesson is read to you, each word lit as it is spoken; later courses hear a real instrument through a microphone or a cable.
featuresPage.cards.lessons.title: Music lessons
featuresPage.cards.offline.body: No account, no telemetry, no network and no model. Every part, fingering and movement comes from rules.
featuresPage.cards.offline.title: Offline, no AI
featuresPage.cards.pianos.body: A grand, an acoustic, an upright and a honky-tonk piano, each with its keys moving as they sound, and played on the same measured piano voices as Freally MIDI Master.
featuresPage.cards.pianos.title: Four real pianos
featuresPage.cards.sheets.body: Chords, melody, countermelody and bass, each on its own sheet, with every note lit as it plays.
featuresPage.cards.sheets.title: Four sheets of music
featuresPage.cards.songs.body: Build a song from sections by hand or start from an artist's arrangement, then mix every part on its own strip, and drag it out with the mix kept.
featuresPage.cards.songs.title: Whole songs and a mixer
featuresPage.cards.strings.body: Acoustic, nylon, electric and muted guitars, fretted, picked and strummed for real, and the bass guitar, played with the fingers and slapped.
featuresPage.cards.strings.title: Guitars and the bass guitar
featuresPage.cards.styles.body: Pick one of 73 genres, 1,507 artists or 833 producers, and the same rule-based generators write the four parts in that style.
featuresPage.cards.styles.title: Every style Freally MIDI Master knows
featuresPage.cards.title: What version 1.0 does
featuresPage.cards.views.body: Switch between them while the music plays; the sheets turn to stay readable and the hands never miss a note.
featuresPage.cards.views.title: Front, overhead and side views
featuresPage.cards.yours.body: Bring in your own audio or MIDI, and Handscore reads it into parts for the hands to play.
featuresPage.cards.yours.title: Your own audio and MIDI
featuresPage.coming.downloads: There are no downloads before version 1.0, and none on this page.
featuresPage.coming.intro: Stated plainly, because a feature list that hides its gaps is not worth reading. This page describes version 1.0, and Handscore is built one version at a time, so most of it is not built yet. Each version on the road to 1.0 is marked with its state.
featuresPage.coming.title: What is still coming
featuresPage.compare.fineprint: Scaler, AR Pianist and Synthesia are the trademarks of their owners, who are not affiliated with Freally Handscore. Tell us if a cell is wrong and we will correct it.
featuresPage.compare.intro: Freally Handscore 1.0 next to the tools people use to write parts or to watch piano played. The other products' cells come from their public listings and reviews, checked in October 2026; where we could not confirm something, the cell says so.
featuresPage.compare.row.drag: Drags the MIDI into your DAW
featuresPage.compare.row.generate: Writes new chords, melodies and basslines in named styles
featuresPage.compare.row.hands: Shows realistic 3D hands playing the notes
featuresPage.compare.row.plugin: Runs inside your DAW as a plugin
featuresPage.compare.row.sheets: Shows the notes as sheet music
featuresPage.compare.summary: Of these four, only Handscore 1.0 has every row: parts written in named styles, realistic hands playing them, the sheet music, the drag into your DAW and the plugin.
featuresPage.compare.theyWin: Scaler 3 is a much broader music-theory workstation. Synthesia is made for learning pieces on your own keyboard; Handscore's lessons listen as you play from version 0.6, but playing along live waits for version 1.9. AR Pianist puts its pianist in your room in augmented reality, which Handscore does not do.
featuresPage.compare.title: Side by side
featuresPage.free.body: Handscore is free today: no paid tier, no subscription and no account. There is nothing to download yet, because there are no downloads before version 1.0.0, and later versions may be sold.
featuresPage.free.title: Free today
featuresPage.lead: Four parts written in any style, shown as sheet music and played by realistic hands on realistic instruments, every part dragged straight into your DAW, and music lessons that teach you to play, write and arrange it yourself.
featuresPage.limits.export: A song whose melody matches a classic or a well-known tune leaves Handscore as its chords only.
featuresPage.limits.families: It plays the pianos, the guitars and the bass guitar. Every other family of instruments arrives one version at a time after 1.0, up to the whole band at 2.0.
featuresPage.limits.learn: Its lessons listen as you play, but the hands do not yet follow you live: playing along on any instrument arrives in version 1.9.
featuresPage.limits.title: What 1.0 does not do
featuresPage.numbers.keys: keys, each named on its front
featuresPage.numbers.parts: parts: chords, melody, countermelody and bass
featuresPage.numbers.plugins: plugin formats, plus a standalone app
featuresPage.version: This page describes what Freally Handscore version 1.0 will do. Today's version is 0.4.0: see the road to 1.0 on the home page.
featuresPage.why.drag.body: The sheets are drawn from the MIDI they drag, and the hands play exactly those notes, so what lands on your track is what you watched.
featuresPage.why.drag.title: What you see is what you drag
featuresPage.why.local.body: No account, no telemetry and no cloud. The plugin and the standalone app never go online, and a build gate fails if networking code is ever added.
featuresPage.why.local.title: It stays on your machine
featuresPage.why.real.body: Every instrument is built to its real measurements: the keyboard is a real piano's size, and every key turns on its balance rail the way a real key does.
featuresPage.why.real.title: Built to real measurements
featuresPage.why.rules.body: Every part, every fingering and every movement comes from rules, with no model anywhere. The same style and the same seed give the same parts, every time.
featuresPage.why.rules.title: Rules, not a model
featuresPage.why.title: Why it is built the way it is

hero.headline: Watch real hands play your music. Then drag it into your DAW.
hero.sub: Chords, a melody, a bassline and a countermelody, written in any style, shown as sheet music and played by realistic hands on realistic instruments, from the piano and the guitar to a whole band. With music lessons that teach you to play, write and arrange it yourself. Offline and 100% AI-free.

honest.network.body: The plugin and the standalone app contain no networking code, and a build gate fails if any is added. A later version may add an update check that stays off unless you switch it on, run by a separate program.
honest.network.title: It never goes online
honest.start.body: Version 0.4.0 loads in a DAW and opens on four real pianos played by realistic hands. Search a genre, an artist or a producer, press Generate, and four parts are written in that style, printed as sheet music on the piano's desk and played by the hands, ready to drag into your DAW, edit note by note or export as MIDI or a PDF. Sixty-two public-domain classics are there to learn, with a transport to pause, rewind and scrub. The overhead and side views, the lessons and every other instrument arrive version by version, as the ladder above shows.

ladder.note: A version that is done is built and tagged. It is not a download: there are none before 1.0.0.
ladder.rung.bass: The bass guitar, played with the fingers and slapped.
ladder.rung.classics: The classics: public-domain tunes to watch and listen to.
ladder.rung.finger-drumming: Finger drumming on a pad controller whose pads light up with every hit, from the first beat to full grooves.
ladder.rung.finish: The finish: settings, eighteen languages throughout, accessibility and the manual.
ladder.rung.guitars: The guitars: acoustic, nylon, electric and muted, with real fretting, picking and strumming.

site.tagline: Watch real hands play your music. Then drag it into your DAW.
what.p1: Most people who use a chord generator never see how its parts would be played, and most people learning an instrument never see a player's hands up close. Handscore shows you both.
what.p2: Pick a genre, an artist or a producer and Handscore writes four parts in that style: chords, a melody, a bassline and a countermelody. They appear as sheets of music on the instrument's stand, and realistic hands play them the way a player of that instrument would: every finger on the key a pianist would use, every fret and strum a guitarist would. The pianos come first, then the guitars and the bass guitar, and after them every family of instruments, up to a whole band.
what.p3: Every note is shown where it is played, each piano key named on its front, so you can see exactly what is sounding. When a part is right, drag it from its sheet straight onto a track in your DAW.
what.p4: And it teaches. The lessons begin on Day 1 at the piano, listen as you play and move on when you have it right, then go on to reading music, rhythm, ear training, theory, songwriting and lyrics, song arrangement, mixing and finger drumming.
